title:
Comment of Sue Ellen Christiansen in Docket(s)/Project(s) P-15423-000
Submission Date: 11/2/2026

documents.name: 152201.txt
documents.text:
Sue Ellen Christiansen, Homer, AK.
Sue Christiansen:
	M

Sue Christiansen:
	There are no underwater data centers of this scale in operation.  Experimenting with our ecosystem and livelihoods is not ok.  The heat and noise, and potential copper pollution, affecting Cook Inlet waters would harm our entire marine food web - from plankton to fish and mammals, including endangered Cook Inlet Beluga (noise threatens their ability to communicate, hunt, navigate, and escape predators).  300 moving tidal turbines in the deep channels that fish and whales (let alone ships) require for passage is not ok.  Where is DeepGreen going to get power during low tides?  No electric utilities have been consulted. Neither Homer Electric Association (HEA), Alaska Power Association (APA), or any other potential utility partner. DeepGreen could require twice the Kenai Peninsula’s average peak energy demand. Are we, the ratepayers, to pay for it?  No, thank you.
Any infrastructure exposed to the Inlet’s strong currents, extreme tides, earthquakes, and difficult weather would require relentless, year-round maintenance in an area absolutely difficult to access.  It poses tremendous ongoing detrimental operational risks.  The most successful seafloor data center created was less than 1% the size of DeepGreen’s proposal. After two years, they pulled their project because of the severe accumulation of microorganisms, plants, algae, and other small aquatic animals.  Cook Inlet waters would provide those exact challenges.  Please, not here, not now, not for big business to prosper and the environment and people that live here to suffer.  Make decisions remembering and honoring the web of life that sustains us. This comment period needs to be extended.  This process was cumbersome, difficult, and rigged.  Who has the time and energy to get through your painstaking process?
